concerns.description: Goal revisions, scene provenance and command decisions
concerns.rationale: Changing observation identity or the logical Mission owner changes the command contract independently of ROS transport.

concerns.description: Hold/Stop behavior, stale observation rejection and command expiry
concerns.rationale: Admissible reactions require a cross-domain mode and freshness contract; event edges do not enforce a stop deadline.

concerns.description: Planner search and ROS service/action adapters
concerns.rationale: Algorithms and transports are replaceable only while goal, feasibility and candidate validity meanings remain fixed.

concerns.description: Executive, GPU planning and isolated onboard stop controller
concerns.rationale: Allocation preserves one logical executive; independent stop-path obligations constrain deployment.

concerns.description: Trajectory integration, geometric collision tests and physical stability
concerns.rationale: Numerical plant evolution and stability require solver semantics and physical assumptions beyond durable fact composition.

facets.meaning: Only a current candidate for the current goal revision may authorize leased motion.
obligations: Realization must compare candidate revision and scene sequence before export.
Clock, freshness threshold and stop latency require measured implementation evidence; no safety guarantee follows from this sidecar.

facets.meaning: Planning overload must not starve command expiry handling.
obligations: Specify queue bounds and scheduling isolation at realization.
Validate watchdog behavior under delayed, duplicated and absent planner results.

realization.strategy: Revision-aware executive with planner and controller adapters; only ReviseMission owns Mission.
realization.placement: Onboard executive and independent local controller; planner may use a GPU.
limitations: No control law, scheduler, WCET analysis or physical safety proof is implemented.
Controller watchdog and coordinate-frame transformations require separate validation.

artifacts.claim: Interface only; no plant simulation, analyzer or safety certification executed.

sources.title: Ptolemy II models of computation
sources.supports: Directors define distinct continuous-time, discrete-event, synchronous/reactive and dataflow laws; typed graph edges alone do not supply them.

sources.title: AUTOSAR Classic Platform
sources.supports: Application, RTE and basic software separation illustrates logical contract versus platform realization; no AUTOSAR conformance claimed.

sources.title: Arcadia method
sources.supports: Logical architecture versus physical architecture supports keeping semantic ownership independent of processor placement.

sources.title: ROS 2 managed node lifecycle
sources.supports: Managed lifecycle states supervise implementation nodes; they are not Mission.mode or a proof of physical safety.
